items.summary: Traditional large language models (LLMs) are scoped to individual user sessions, limiting their knowledge to a single conversation and preventing them from learning user preferences that evolve over time. Existing agentic memory systems address this limitation but generally operate at the individual-user level, restricting the public knowledge that could be shared across users to improve downstream responses. We introduce AIM (Agentic Interoperable Memory), a unified, privacy-aware memory framework that enables multi-agent, multi-user LLM systems to persistently manage private and shared memory. AIM dynamically classifies information as private, scoped to one user and inaccessible to others, or public, accessible to all users. It enforces index-level access controls so that private memories are retrievable only by their owner, protecting sensitive data while allowing beneficial shared knowledge to improve coordination and consistency. We also introduce MUMBench (Multi-User Memory Benchmark), a dataset of multi-user interactions containing private and shareable information across four domains. To our knowledge, MUMBench is the first public dataset designed to evaluate multiple memory operations, including retrieval, creation, update, and deletion, in a multi-user environment. Across three independent runs on MUMBench, AIM achieves 96.0% visibility classification accuracy, 58.8% strict operation accuracy, and 70.5% state-aware operation accuracy.
items.title: AIM: A Privacy-Aware Interoperable Memory Framework for Multi-Agent Multi-User LLM Systems

items.summary: This work considers multi-agent coordination with arbitrary information networks among the agents using a game-theoretic approach. A system designer aims to assign local utility functions to the agents to guide their actions toward a desired system objective. The performance of the assigned local utilities is measured by the well known pure price of anarchy (pPoA) metric that equals the ratio of the system objective at the worst pure Nash equilibrium of the corresponding game to the optimal system objective. Our aim is to derive the utility functions which optimize the pPoA-based performance guarantees for any given information network and system objective. We develop a linear program that derives the optimal pPoA for any arbitrary information network and arbitrary system objective. Our work is the first to solve optimal utility design for arbitrary networks; our techniques generalize previous approaches which considered only the full-information setting. For supermodular objective functions, we prove that counterintuitively, a fully communication-denied utility design is optimal irrespective of the original information network. For submodular system objectives, an exhaustive numerical analysis suggests that the optimal utility design is robust to communication failures even for this case. When the system objective is weighted maximum coverage, the marginal contribution utility design provably optimizes the pPoA for a wide variety of information networks of interest.
items.title: Deriving the Pure Price of Anarchy for Networked Resource Allocation Games

items.summary: Lux AI Season 3 requires agents to act under partial observability, randomized episode level dynamics, and a best of five match structure that rewards both tactical execution and fast adaptation. We present HORIZON, a hierarchical agent that combines symmetry aware spatial perception, dual memory belief tracking, relic centric graph attention, information gain driven exploration, and an opponent conditioned policy mixture. HORIZON separates short horizon control from cross match meta reasoning, while auxiliary belief and world model objectives stabilize learning. Trained with PPO in a large scale JAX simulator, the resulting agent explicitly infers hidden game parameters and opponent style. Experiments show consistent gains in match win rate, episode win rate, adaptation gain, and league rating over strong recurrent and feed forward baselines.
items.title: Hierarchical Belief Modeling for Zero-Shot Opponent Adaptation in Partially Observable Multi-Agent Navigation

items.summary: The Earth That Heard   The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua's altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel's unfinished offering, Cain's failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. This version adds a new chapter on Cain, the altar, and the city of refuge — linking "from My altar you shall take him" (Exodus 21:14) to the Mishnah's ruling that one sentenced without a High Priest never goes free (Makkot 2:7), and to the discovery that Shechem itself is designated a city of refuge in Joshua 20:7. Additional sections trace Jacob's route from Sukkot to Shechem as a draft of Joshua's entry axis, the letter-midrash of "sotho" (Genesis 49:11) as a covering that was never performed, and the mechanical letter-echo of Shaddai hidden in Laban's Aramaic "Yegar Sahadutha" (Genesis 31:47).12:56 PM   The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place, 100,000 permutations yield T1 = 11.23 and T2 = 24.12, with zero exceedances (p_MC ≈ 10⁻⁵; Phipson & Smyth, 2010). A Leave-One-Book-Out test shows no single Torah book is necessary for the signal (worst case: Genesis removed → Z = 10.61). A Leave-One-Motif-Out test shows no single root is necessary (worst: rbtz removed → Z = 16.01). A book-stratified null (Z = 19.93) confirms the effect is not an artifact of verse distribution. A top-10 ablation (Z = 3.95, p = 0.0013) shows the signal weakens but survives removal of the dominant motifs. A Foundation 12-Letter Split, stripping all 10 control letters rather than 7, yields Z = 4.17 — confirming the framework is not ad-hoc. Six benchmark anthologies were tested: the Ebal/Shechem axis is anomalous in all three validated methods; Covenant remains a positive control but significantly lower; Joseph, Tabernacle, and "the place that He will choose" are negative in all. An independent replication pilot tested whether the signal depends on the author's specific verse choices. Eight semantic criteria were defined — no roots, no letter analysis, no knowledge of any test results — and two independent language models selected Torah verses blind. Model A (243 verses) yielded T2 = 8.70; Model B (252 verses) yielded T2 = 9.84; the consensus of both (142 verses) yielded T2 = 8.51. All with zero exceedances. Only 22% of the essay's verses were also selected. The signal survives independent selection. A pre-registered protocol for three independent human readers is included (protocol hash: a577cb03...). The result does not statistically prove the theological interpretation; it shows that the textual concentration being interpreted is itself measurable and unusual under multiple independent approaches. A dual adversarial computational audit (LLM-assisted) verified the code, reproduced the numbers, identified and corrected all bugs, and rated the statistical appendix at 7.0

items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems, jointly interpreting images and natural language queries, hold significant promise across many domains, yet the privacy-sensitive nature of user data creates a fundamental barrier. Centralized training requires access to all data, while federated learning requires each client to host the full model. We propose USPLIT-VQA, a U-shaped split learning framework for privacy-preserving VQA in which each client retains the initial layers and the classification head while the server hosts the computationally heavy intermediate layers, keeping raw inputs and labels on the client device. We further introduce Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation (CAWA), a gradientsimilarity-based client scoring mechanism designed to reduce the influence of malicious updates. Experiments on four VQA datasets (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PathVQA, and VizWiz) with two backbones show accuracy gains over Federated Learning for the Custom model and reduced accuracy for BiomedCLIP under the evaluated fixed split, alongside client memory reductions of up to 5.8X and communication reductions of up to 10.8X. With one malicious client, CAWA reduces the attacker's influence by over 98%, while experiments at higher corruption levels identify its limitations. Reconstruction experiments further show lower inversion quality under the evaluated attacks.
items.title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation

items.summary: ADR1D is a reproducible synthetic benchmark for one-dimensional advection-dispersion-reaction transport. It contains 300 parameterized scenarios, 749,700 analytical space-time concentration records, and 88,200 noisy virtual-sensor observations. Fixed scenario-level training, validation, and test partitions support leakage-aware forward, inverse, reconstruction, and arrival-detection studies. The release includes the complete generation configuration, a machine-readable data dictionary, dependency-free Python generation and validation scripts, and validation records.
items.title: ADR1D: A Reproducible One-Dimensional Advection-Dispersion-Reaction Benchmark Dataset

items.summary: Higher-order regularization has shown improved results over first-order methods such as total variation. In this paper, convergence of a piecewise linear finite element discretization is shown for the second-order total generalized variation functional. Additionally, this convergence result is extended to a spatiotemporal setting after the spatiotemporal function space is comprehensively introduced. In both cases, discrete minimizers converge to the continuous minimizer with rate $h^{1/4}$, matching the best known rate for finite element discretizations of total variation in the same general setting. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence rates and indicate faster convergence in practice. Comparisons with related spatial image reconstruction algorithms show comparable reconstruction results. The spatiotemporal case is discussed using the example of the inverse problem in electrocardiographic imaging, where the proposed functional improves the state of the art.
items.title: Total Generalized Variation for Inverse Problems Involving Piecewise Linear Finite Elements

items.summary: Bridge assessment treats inspection, structural analysis and damage identification as sequential, separated steps. Concealed damage is assumed based on indirect information resulting in speculative values. An integrated, cloud-based workflow that automates the pipeline from drone-acquired point clouds to damage-aware BIM/FEM analysis and nondestructive concealed damage identification is introduced, which accelerates the overall process and provides a real as-is degraded bridge model, which provides reliable bridge assessment. The total process is designed as a highly automated BIMification process and implemented in the cloud with one access point, which speeds up the whole process. The process is presented in two parts. Part 1 covers the reconstruction of the geometrical BIM model from the measured point cloud obtained by UAV-based RGB and LiDAR observations, whereas in this paper, Part 2 introduces concealed damage identification by applying an inverse simulation-based damage analysis. The simulation-based system identification compares computed deformations of candidate damage models with observed deformations, while beforehand a robust sensitivity analysis identifies system-relevant damages, which are then considered. A distributed asynchronous task queue orchestrates large-scale, parallel computation of remote generation of damage variants, automated execution of structural analyses, post-processing, and creation of evaluation results. The platform readily integrates with web frameworks and common brokers and supports concurrent execution. A case study with a real motorway-bridge demonstrates that the proposed new damage identification method, automation and cloudification markedly accelerate assessment and enable prompt, reliable estimation of residual structural capacity, closing a critical gap in post-event safety evaluation.
items.title: From Drone Observed Bridge Displacements to Concealed Damage Identification and Assessment

items.summary: Differentiable Photon Transport — Volume I: Foundations , by Chris von Csefalvay, is an instructional book on differentiable photon transport using X-ray and C-arm imaging. Version 1.0.0 includes the public book source and a built static website. The website archive preserves the interactive figures, recorded numerical display data and source listings. items.summary: The contemporary discourse of "media ethics" rests on a terminological error. The corpus keyword is FREE SPEECH — the first liberty of the Gordon–Trenchard tradition (Cato's Letters, 1720–23) — not the later, softer vocabulary of media ethics, which presupposes a neutral structure that does not exist. Media is not neutral structure; it is an appetite. This essay distinguishes authentic free speech (civic speech addressed to communities about matters of common concern) from its three principal perversions — the speech of warmongers, pornographers, and advertisers — and documents the claim through a fifty-year publishing record: Media Free Times: A Random Sampling of Anarchic Communications Art (1972–present), a multimedia periodical operating across microfilm, audio cassette, and print, with production and preservation processes developed in direct experimental exchange with Library and Archives Canada in the 1970s. The essay records the free-speech-movement origins at San Jose State under Prof. Phil Jacqueline, the first Free Speech Messages (FSM) broadcasts via the Bay Area Committee for Public Access, the Virtual Free University concept and its anticipatory cross-media date index, and the documented lifecycle of archival suppression at Library and Archives Canada — including the reconstruction that was once coherent and fully linked, with the archive itself on record calling it a precursor of web pages. The transition from open-source FSM to closed-loop TED is named info dysinformation architecture: the architecture retained, the openness excised. The remedy proposed is twofold — restoration of the free-speech vocabulary and systematic recovery, in the twelve-step tradition, from the engineered appetites (sucrose, spectacle, surveillance) that make the perversion economy profitable. Keywords: free speech; media ethics; info dysinformation architecture; FSM; TED; Media Free Times; Virtual Free University; Media Anonymous; sucrose; attention commons; Cato's Letters; propaganda; Jacques Ellul; Neil Postman; data preservation; copper sheets
items.title: MEDIA ETHICS AND FREE SPEECH — OR THE LACK THEREOF From Open-Source FSM to Closed-Loop TED, and the Recovery of the First Liberty

items.summary: Clinical timelines support treatment-window analysis and leakage-free modeling, but discharge summaries often obscure chronology and structured EHR tables describe only part of the patient course. We present a UID-preserving framework that links each narrative event occurrence to its source span and retains that identity through text-only estimation, structured-evidence retrieval, timestamped source-row grounding, and joint revision. We also present GAVEL, an LLM judge that compares two UID-aligned timelines against the narrative and structured record, to augment prior matching and temporal assessments. Across six open-weight models and 40 mixed-critical-care summaries, the GLM 5.2 multimodal revision, as compared to its text-only variant, improved temporal agreement without reducing event recovery and performed competitively with clinician annotations, while other model revisions showed smaller gains and lower overall performance. Ablations showed that UIDs primarily preserve event retention, whereas source-row linkage supports temporal placement. Blinded human review upheld most GAVEL findings, and controlled adjudication favored multimodal over text-only GLM 5.2 but did not for DeepSeek V3.2. In developing the UID and judge pipeline, we are able to demonstrate 43\% increased event recovery, a framework competitive with clinician annotations, and a system with occurrence-level provenance for both reconstruction and evaluation.
items.title: Anchoring Clinical Events in Time: UID-Preserving Multimodal Reconstruction and Source-Grounded Adjudication

items.summary: nifti2dicom 2.1.0 A shared, tested conversion pipeline for scalar 2D/3D/4D CT, MR and classic PET, binary/multilabel DICOM SEG, and 2D/3D RGB Secondary Capture. Highlights Physical-coordinate geometry and explicit temporal correspondence replace vendor-specific flips. PET uses per-image quantitative encoding. Real-data fixes cover reversed native PET indexing, sagittal dynamic MR acquisition metadata, series-uniform metadata and conditional DICOM tags. One public conversion/inspection API, clearer CLI errors, JSON reports and staged output publication with overwrite recovery. Optional Slicer 5.12 PET integration preserves dynamic timing, geometry and decoded values in both Sequences and MultiVolumes. Clean source/wheel boundaries, automated test/build/archive checks and versioned GitHub-release-to-PyPI publishing. Validation The final conversion code passed 827 package tests, 135 pure Slicer tests and 15 native Slicer regressions. Fifteen IDC series were independently reconstructed and checked: 291,257,888 voxels, 10,910 output images, zero dciodvfy errors. Eight public Slicer imports and binary/multilabel SEG regressions passed. See the detailed evidence . Upgrade notes Existing output fails clearly unless --overwrite is requested. Vendor-specific flipping is removed; the deprecated vendor argument is ignored. SEG requires truthful algorithm provenance. Provide algorithm name/version for automatic or semiautomatic masks; conversion is not mask inference. Numeric overflow is reported or quantitatively rescaled, never silently clipped. Generated images use stable IM_000001.dcm filenames. Read result.files or *.dcm : each output directory also contains conversion.json . See the README for current commands and compatibility notes. Scope This is engineering validation, not clinical certification or universal viewer compatibility. MR uses documented standard-extended rescaling attributes; strict base-IOD findings remain disclosed. Enhanced/gated PET and overlapping, probabilistic or time-varying SEG are not supported. Quantization is bounded, not universally lossless. Receiver acceptance and truthful input provenance remain necessary.
items.title: ENHANCE-PET/nifti2dicom: nifti2dicom 2.1.0

items.summary: Code, trained model artifacts, processed result tables, public-input manifests and figure source data supporting the manuscript "FORGE audits residue-level information encoded in RNA tertiary-structure geometry". The release contains the FORGE feature-extraction and analysis code, trained XGBoost model files for nucleotide identity and auxiliary atlas tasks, locked result artifacts used by the manuscript figures and tables, and manifests for the public PDB/Rfam/OpenKnot-derived inputs. Raw PDB/mmCIF coordinate caches and full third-party software repositories are not redistributed; they are identified by accession/source manifests and can be retrieved from their original public repositories. Version 0.2.0 adds the AlphaFold 3 forward-folding control supporting the Nature Machine Intelligence resubmission: raw AlphaFold 3 server job outputs for the four solved AI-designed pseudoknot constructs (real, FORGE-derived and R-Net-refined sequence classes), batch job requests, fine-grained comparison metrics (P-RMSD, secondary-structure F1, contact recovery), R-Net-guided refinement artifacts, forward-folding figures and the NMI manuscript LaTeX source.

items.summary: Circular economy is the trend that has emerged as an urgent necessity for manufacturing companies trying to break the linear "take, make, dispose" production cycle. While there is a significant amount of research happening in the circularity domain, the body of knowledge is split and does not necessarily connect with other theories, concepts and with application in different industrial sectors. The aim of this study was to develop an integrated conceptual framework to overcome the existing ambiguities in the field of CE and to facilitate further research while synthesizing the various streams of research on the topic. Methods: The articles were systematically identified from Web of Science and Scopus databases, and then snowballing was performed, in compliance with the PRISMA guidelines, between 2010 and 2025, and resulted in the identification of 100 articles. A tripartite analytical technique based on the use of quantitative bibliometric analysis, qualitative bibliographic content analysis and conceptual mapping was used. Results: The major thematic clusters that emerged were: circular supply chains, design for circularity, industrial symbiosis, Industry 4.0 enablers, policy and governance, performance measurement. The key practices of CE were identified and categorized according to the 4R and 10R frameworks, reverse logistics, industrial symbiosis and digital support for resource recovery at the micro, meso and macro level. The analysis shows that there are organizational, financial, technological and regulatory challenges that remain unaddressed, and that there is a significant lack of empirical evidence on a larger scale. Conclusions: There is a coherent conceptual framework linking CE principles with supply chain operations and Industry 4.0 technologies in this review and it proposes a prioritized future research direction that covers eight critical knowledge gaps. Government, industry and academia receive practical guidance on how to speed circular transitions in manufacturing.
tags: Circular economy, manufacturing, systematic literature review, supply chain management, Industry 4.0, PRISMA, reverse logistics, sustainability, resource recovery, 4R framework
items.title: Circular Economy in Manufacturing Industries: A Literature Review and Future Research Agenda

items.summary: Reproducibility package supporting an analysis of sustainability transition in Sarawak, Malaysia. The repository contains curated analytical and processed datasets, acquisition and processing notebooks, model outputs, robustness analyses, figures, quality-assurance records, provenance documentation and detailed reproduction guidance. The research examines whether low-carbon development constitutes a sustainability transition when ecological integrity, biodiversity and climate-conditioned environmental vulnerability are considered alongside energy and development outcomes. The package contains 103 scientific files together with repository control documentation. Eleven public-facing scientific files were prepared as portability-safe or publication-safe copies without changing the underlying scientific results. Three RQ5 outputs carry explicit provenance warnings because their original computational specification could not be fully reconstructed; these limitations are transparently documented. Third-party and derived datasets remain governed by their original licensing and attribution terms.

items.summary: Analysis code, derived result tables, figures and the pre-specified analysis plan for a study of direction-consistent differential gene expression between non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (GSE89632, GSE126848) and bladder urothelial carcinoma (TCGA-BLCA). Contains the complete pipeline in Python, the output and provenance record of every stage, the full direction-consistent gene table and enrichment table untruncated, and the analysis plan with its thresholds fixed before any data were examined together with the amendments made afterwards. Raw input data is not included: all three datasets are public and are better obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus and the NCI Genomic Data Commons. The provenance files record exactly which files were retrieved, when, and with what checksums. items.summary: The book series The Stream and the Algebra presents a speculative research programme — a thought-experiment in the mathematics of relation, offered for scrutiny, not yet peer-reviewed or tested. Its wager: nothing physical is an absolute number (a mass means nothing until a unit is chosen), only how one quantity stands to another. It fixes the dimensionless relations the world determines and concedes one scale, the anchor; a firewall shares a structure's form across domains, never a bare number. Its sharpest stakes: an axion-free zero of strong CP, few-GeV asymmetric dark matter, and the tau mass from Koide read forward. From the fundamental particles it carries this idea to the vacuum, the classical world, and physics' open problems. Book VII asks where the flavour geometry comes from. items.summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Images in the public archives use standardized identifiers and filenames such as BDVLP_000001.jpg. Original source filenames are preserved in the metadata manifest for provenance and reproducibility. The image packaging procedure preserves the original source image bytes and does not resize or re-encode the images. BanglaVLP-5K is released as an annotation-free curated raw-image dataset. It does not include manually verified licence-plate bounding boxes, licence-plate character transcriptions, or manually verified vehicle-category ground-truth labels. Any automatically generated vehicle-category estimates present in the metadata are provided only as auxiliary technical descriptors and must not be interpreted as verified annotations or ground-truth labels. The dataset may be useful for computer vision research, vehicle and traffic-scene analysis, domain adaptation, transfer learning, image-quality and robustness studies, development and evaluation of image-processing methods, and the creation of future manually annotated derivative datasets for vehicle or licence-plate-related research. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.
items.title: BanglaVLP-5K: A Curated High-Resolution Image Dataset of Bangladeshi Vehicles and Licence Plates in Real-World Traffic Environments

items.summary: This record contains the cumulative Lean-verified Chronos dimensionality and Möbius-field formalization from M1 through M6. The work formally separates a scalar temporal point-state from the dimensionality of the ambient coordinate space and from the scalar field defined over that space. In the verified construction, the Chronos x-value remains a scalar state, while spatial dimensionality is carried independently by explicitly typed Euclidean coordinate spaces. This makes the distinction between field state and coordinate dimension precise and machine-checkable. The M1–M6 chain begins with the Möbius sign-reversal structure, including one-lap orientation reversal, two-lap state recovery, and the continuous zero-crossing result. It then introduces the exact dimensional field architecture, allowing the same scalar point-state to be represented in one-dimensional, three-dimensional, and generic finite-dimensional fields without identifying the scalar value itself with a dimension. The later milestones prove exact transfer of the one-dimensional temporal profile into arbitrary-dimensional scalar fields, radial specialization of that construction, and the resulting dimension-dependent geometry of constant-state level sets. In three spatial dimensions, the exact Chronos x-state is formally identified with a spherical level shell inside the previously verified radial gravity field. The series further proves the exact field gradient and gradient-coupled acceleration on the x-shell, preserves the established Newtonian correspondence under the stated gravity calibration, and extends the construction to moving x-level shells and time-indexed radial fields. The final milestone establishes a generic dynamic radial-gradient theorem for arbitrary differentiable evolving radial profiles. The result shows formally how a local radial field slope determines the corresponding spatial gradient and gradient-coupled acceleration, including exact zero-response and opposite-slope response theorems. The complete M1–M6 dependency chain kernel-checked successfully against the pinned OpenAI NavierStokesAndEuler environment. The cumulative build completed 9,327 Lake jobs. Thirty-seven explicit axiom checks were performed. The audited declarations depend only on standard Lean/Mathlib foundational principles and contain no project-specific axioms, sorry , admit , or sorryAx proof placeholders. This formalization proves the dimensional field architecture and its stated consequences. It establishes that scalar temporal state and ambient coordinate dimension are mathematically distinct objects and proves how one scalar state lifts into dimension-dependent field geometry. A later formal target is to derive or select dimensional structure dynamically rather than supplying the coordinate dimension as an index. The archive includes Lean source, reproducibility scripts, verification logs, axiom audits, deterministic numerical checks, provenance information, checksums, and milestone documentation.

items.summary: This dataset and replication package accompanies a comparative spatial-network analysis of the structural resilience of international digital connectivity across the 32 NATO member states and Russia. The study integrates active international submarine communication cable (SCC) systems with operational cross-border terrestrial fibre connectivity (LCC) and evaluates how much direct external-partner connectivity remains under progressively more severe disruption scenarios. The principal outcome is Partner Retention, defined as the share of baseline direct external partners that remain connected after a disruption. The analysis includes random SCC failures, geographically correlated disruption, complete SCC outage, terrestrial partner concentration tests, alternative clustering thresholds, and additional robustness checks. Under a complete submarine-cable outage, Russia retains 92.3% of its direct external partners, compared with a median of 33.3% among NATO members with active submarine-cable connectivity. The results indicate that this structural advantage is primarily associated with Russia’s extensive cross-border terrestrial fibre network rather than a larger submarine-cable system. The package includes R scripts, processed replication data, selected raw submarine-cable inputs, result tables, figures, QGIS outputs, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, metadata, and methodological notes. The dataset measures structural connectivity rather than traffic volume, bandwidth, latency, economic loss, repair time, or dynamic rerouting capacity.
items.title: Structural Resilience of International Digital Connectivity under Submarine Cable Disruption: NATO Members and Russia

items.summary: Production artificial intelligence systems are increasingly assessed not only by whether they generate accurate predictions, but by whether the operating organization can reconstruct, explain, and defend the exact evidence behind an individual outcome after the surrounding system has changed. This paper develops a quantitative framework for measuring that property, which we term evidence continuity. The framework is grounded primarily and foundationally in the work of Mesbaul Haque Sazu, specifically his Governed Decision-Intelligence (GDI) reference architecture [22] and his Full-Stack Production-Platform Reference Architecture [21]. GDI establishes the decision as the unit of assurance and makes evidence binding, lineage, validation, calibrated confidence, deterministic explanation, human oversight, and outcome closure explicit control obligations. The Full-Stack architecture extends these obligations into runtime operation through capture-at-commit, execution records, trajectory-level observability, before-commit gating, and closed-loop production control. Building directly on and leveraging these two foundations, this paper contributes a measurement layer that sits above them. We model an AI system as a typed, versioned, directed evidence graph and introduce three constructs: the Evidence Continuity Graph (ECG), the Trace Completeness Ratio (TCR), and the Governance Coverage Index (GCI). We formalize per-decision and aggregate estimators, extend the naive independence model to a correlated-failure regime using a Beta-Binomial mixture, and derive path-based reconstructability over admissible evidence paths. A synthetic benchmark of 2,800 investigation traces demonstrates how time-to-trace, incomplete-trace probability, and reconstruction probability respond as evidence coverage varies. The results are illustrative rather than empirical claims about deployed systems. The paper concludes with a reference implementation architecture, threshold-setting guidance calibrated to deployment risk, a security and failure analysis, and a research agenda for validating evidence continuity on real production workloads.

items.summary: This work considers multi-agent coordination with arbitrary information networks among the agents using a game-theoretic approach. A system designer aims to assign local utility functions to the agents to guide their actions toward a desired system objective. The performance of the assigned local utilities is measured by the well known pure price of anarchy (pPoA) metric that equals the ratio of the system objective at the worst pure Nash equilibrium of the corresponding game to the optimal system objective. Our aim is to derive the utility functions which optimize the pPoA-based performance guarantees for any given information network and system objective. We develop a linear program that derives the optimal pPoA for any arbitrary information network and arbitrary system objective. Our work is the first to solve optimal utility design for arbitrary networks; our techniques generalize previous approaches which considered only the full-information setting. For supermodular objective functions, we prove that counterintuitively, a fully communication-denied utility design is optimal irrespective of the original information network. For submodular system objectives, an exhaustive numerical analysis suggests that the optimal utility design is robust to communication failures even for this case. When the system objective is weighted maximum coverage, the marginal contribution utility design provably optimizes the pPoA for a wide variety of information networks of interest.
items.title: Deriving the Pure Price of Anarchy for Networked Resource Allocation Games

items.summary: The Earth That Heard   The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua's altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel's unfinished offering, Cain's failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. This version adds a new chapter on Cain, the altar, and the city of refuge — linking "from My altar you shall take him" (Exodus 21:14) to the Mishnah's ruling that one sentenced without a High Priest never goes free (Makkot 2:7), and to the discovery that Shechem itself is designated a city of refuge in Joshua 20:7. Additional sections trace Jacob's route from Sukkot to Shechem as a draft of Joshua's entry axis, the letter-midrash of "sotho" (Genesis 49:11) as a covering that was never performed, and the mechanical letter-echo of Shaddai hidden in Laban's Aramaic "Yegar Sahadutha" (Genesis 31:47).12:56 PM   The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place, 100,000 permutations yield T1 = 11.23 and T2 = 24.12, with zero exceedances (p_MC ≈ 10⁻⁵; Phipson & Smyth, 2010). A Leave-One-Book-Out test shows no single Torah book is necessary for the signal (worst case: Genesis removed → Z = 10.61). A Leave-One-Motif-Out test shows no single root is necessary (worst: rbtz removed → Z = 16.01). A book-stratified null (Z = 19.93) confirms the effect is not an artifact of verse distribution. A top-10 ablation (Z = 3.95, p = 0.0013) shows the signal weakens but survives removal of the dominant motifs. A Foundation 12-Letter Split, stripping all 10 control letters rather than 7, yields Z = 4.17 — confirming the framework is not ad-hoc. Six benchmark anthologies were tested: the Ebal/Shechem axis is anomalous in all three validated methods; Covenant remains a positive control but significantly lower; Joseph, Tabernacle, and "the place that He will choose" are negative in all. An independent replication pilot tested whether the signal depends on the author's specific verse choices. Eight semantic criteria were defined — no roots, no letter analysis, no knowledge of any test results — and two independent language models selected Torah verses blind. Model A (243 verses) yielded T2 = 8.70; Model B (252 verses) yielded T2 = 9.84; the consensus of both (142 verses) yielded T2 = 8.51. All with zero exceedances. Only 22% of the essay's verses were also selected. The signal survives independent selection. A pre-registered protocol for three independent human readers is included (protocol hash: a577cb03...). The result does not statistically prove the theological interpretation; it shows that the textual concentration being interpreted is itself measurable and unusual under multiple independent approaches. A dual adversarial computational audit (LLM-assisted) verified the code, reproduced the numbers, identified and corrected all bugs, and rated the statistical appendix at 7.0

items.summary: The book series The Stream and the Algebra presents a speculative research programme — a thought-experiment in the mathematics of relation, offered for scrutiny, not yet peer-reviewed or tested. Its wager: nothing physical is an absolute number (a mass means nothing until a unit is chosen), only how one quantity stands to another. It fixes the dimensionless relations the world determines and concedes one scale, the anchor; a firewall shares a structure's form across domains, never a bare number. Its sharpest stakes: an axion-free zero of strong CP, few-GeV asymmetric dark matter, and the tau mass from Koide read forward. From the fundamental particles it carries this idea to the vacuum, the classical world, and physics' open problems. Book VII asks where the flavour geometry comes from. It fixes one concrete, frozen heterotic string vacuum — a Z_6-II orbifold of the E_8×E_8 mini-landscape, its provenance settled before any measured number is consulted — and asks whether the single amplitude the Koide relation leaves free descends from it. The programme holds throughout to one firewall: a structure's form may cross domains, a bare number never; and it keeps the line between what the mathematics closes and what stays open. No physical grade is raised; the Koide value stays open. Book VII is issued at one frozen epoch as three parts under a single manifest and version stamp — Part VII.1 (Corpus & Conditional Layers), Part VII.2 (the monograph edition) and Part VII.3 (the internal Annexes: the Ω-sections and the revision history). Part VII.3, The Source and the Cube: The Annexes, is the append-only provenance record behind Book VII — the hundreds of dated Ω-findings, the routes tried and refuted, the corrections booked with banners, and the full revision chronicle. It is not a publication of record and is never the sole terminal support of a claim typed closed: it is the working behind Parts VII.1 and VII.2, hash-frozen and available on request. Its discipline is the firewall in action. Every finding carries a typed Grade block with B_3=0 throughout — no physical grade raised anywhere — and superseded claims are retained with inline supersession banners rather than deleted. The record documents the successive self- corrections that led to the current readings: the group-identity restoration to SmallGroup(648,597); the Koide rank correction, in which the earlier rank-2 reading K=2/3 at Kähler ratio ≈ 14 was recognised as the rank-two crossing (2+sqrt(3))^2 artefact and resolved in the source's favour to a genuine rank-3 three-mass landing; the mirror factorisation g(1+i)=2^1/4e^-iπ/24; and the strong-CP finite-representation phase (Φ_3=π present for the minimal Standard-Model colour sector — the modular symmetry does not by itself protect strong CP). It also carries the cross-pollination glosses toward the closed Books I–VI: the sqrt(2) read as a level-2 modular reflection value refining Book I's Pythagorean reading; the Fricke mirror confirming Book V's duality, not symmetry; and the rank-3 typing sharpening the conditional Koide of Books II and IV. items.summary: This dataset and replication package accompanies a comparative spatial-network analysis of the structural resilience of international digital connectivity across the 32 NATO member states and Russia. The study integrates active international submarine communication cable (SCC) systems with operational cross-border terrestrial fibre connectivity (LCC) and evaluates how much direct external-partner connectivity remains under progressively more severe disruption scenarios. The principal outcome is Partner Retention, defined as the share of baseline direct external partners that remain connected after a disruption. The analysis includes random SCC failures, geographically correlated disruption, complete SCC outage, terrestrial partner concentration tests, alternative clustering thresholds, and additional robustness checks. Under a complete submarine-cable outage, Russia retains 92.3% of its direct external partners, compared with a median of 33.3% among NATO members with active submarine-cable connectivity. The results indicate that this structural advantage is primarily associated with Russia’s extensive cross-border terrestrial fibre network rather than a larger submarine-cable system. The package includes R scripts, processed replication data, selected raw submarine-cable inputs, result tables, figures, QGIS outputs, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, metadata, and methodological notes. The dataset measures structural connectivity rather than traffic volume, bandwidth, latency, economic loss, repair time, or dynamic rerouting capacity.
items.title: Structural Resilience of International Digital Connectivity under Submarine Cable Disruption: NATO Members and Russia

items.summary: This replication package contains the data, R scripts, figures, and documentation used in the study “Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025.” The study examines the temporal structure of naval procurement competition between Turkey and Greece using annual data for 1990–2025. The main empirical series are derived from the SIPRI Arms Transfers Database and SIPRI Transfer Register. Annual Ships Trend Indicator Value (TIV) data are used to measure international naval platform deliveries, while order-year information is used to distinguish procurement decisions from subsequent deliveries. World Bank World Development Indicators are used for the macroeconomic control variable. The analysis tests contemporaneous and 1–3-year lagged relationships between Greek and Turkish naval procurement. Robustness checks include Newey–West HAC standard errors, alternative bandwidths, leave-one-out tests, influential-year exclusions, winsorization, placebo leads, and multiple-testing corrections using the Benjamini–Hochberg, Holm, and Bonferroni procedures. All data preparation and statistical analyses were conducted in R. The results show that Turkish and Greek naval procurement processes are temporally connected rather than independent. The strongest delivery-to-delivery association appears at a two-year lag. Greek naval deliveries are also associated with Turkish international naval orders one year later, while reverse-direction models identify associations between Turkish deliveries and subsequent Greek international orders. The overall pattern is consistent with reciprocal and temporally clustered modernization cycles rather than a fixed one-way action–reaction process. The repository includes cleaned analytical datasets, R scripts, figures, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, citation metadata, and the manuscript. Raw proprietary or redistribution-restricted source files are not included; users should consult the original SIPRI and World Bank sources where applicable. Version 1.2 adds the reviewer-requested stationarity diagnostics, first-difference sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-programme-window-out tests. The revised package also includes updated regression outputs and the reviewer-revised manuscript. The main research design and core delivery-to-delivery finding remain unchanged.
items.title: Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025: Replication Data and Code

items.summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Images in the public archives use standardized identifiers and filenames such as BDVLP_000001.jpg. Original source filenames are preserved in the metadata manifest for provenance and reproducibility. The image packaging procedure preserves the original source image bytes and does not resize or re-encode the images. BanglaVLP-5K is released as an annotation-free curated raw-image dataset. It does not include manually verified licence-plate bounding boxes, licence-plate character transcriptions, or manually verified vehicle-category ground-truth labels. Any automatically generated vehicle-category estimates present in the metadata are provided only as auxiliary technical descriptors and must not be interpreted as verified annotations or ground-truth labels. The dataset may be useful for computer vision research, vehicle and traffic-scene analysis, domain adaptation, transfer learning, image-quality and robustness studies, development and evaluation of image-processing methods, and the creation of future manually annotated derivative datasets for vehicle or licence-plate-related research. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.
items.title: BanglaVLP-5K: A Curated High-Resolution Image Dataset of Bangladeshi Vehicles and Licence Plates in Real-World Traffic Environments

items.summary: Production artificial intelligence systems are increasingly assessed not only by whether they generate accurate predictions, but by whether the operating organization can reconstruct, explain, and defend the exact evidence behind an individual outcome after the surrounding system has changed. This paper develops a quantitative framework for measuring that property, which we term evidence continuity. The framework is grounded primarily and foundationally in the work of Mesbaul Haque Sazu, specifically his Governed Decision-Intelligence (GDI) reference architecture [22] and his Full-Stack Production-Platform Reference Architecture [21]. GDI establishes the decision as the unit of assurance and makes evidence binding, lineage, validation, calibrated confidence, deterministic explanation, human oversight, and outcome closure explicit control obligations. The Full-Stack architecture extends these obligations into runtime operation through capture-at-commit, execution records, trajectory-level observability, before-commit gating, and closed-loop production control. Building directly on and leveraging these two foundations, this paper contributes a measurement layer that sits above them. We model an AI system as a typed, versioned, directed evidence graph and introduce three constructs: the Evidence Continuity Graph (ECG), the Trace Completeness Ratio (TCR), and the Governance Coverage Index (GCI). We formalize per-decision and aggregate estimators, extend the naive independence model to a correlated-failure regime using a Beta-Binomial mixture, and derive path-based reconstructability over admissible evidence paths. A synthetic benchmark of 2,800 investigation traces demonstrates how time-to-trace, incomplete-trace probability, and reconstruction probability respond as evidence coverage varies. The results are illustrative rather than empirical claims about deployed systems. The paper concludes with a reference implementation architecture, threshold-setting guidance calibrated to deployment risk, a security and failure analysis, and a research agenda for validating evidence continuity on real production workloads.

items.summary: Overview  This repository contains the dataset, preprocessing pipeline, surrogate model training scripts, NSGA-II multi-objective optimization suite, and raw experimental outputs supporting the manuscript: "A Leakage-Controlled CatBoost–NSGA-II Framework for Concrete Mix Design: Evaluation Protocol and Strength-Floor Sensitivity" Abstract Traditional concrete mix design usually involves lengthy empirical trial-and-error procedures. This study proposes a CatBoost–NSGA-II framework for multi-objective optimisation of concrete mixes, including leakage-controlled evaluation, uncertainty-aware strength feasibility, repeated-run robustness, and strength-floor sensitivity analysis. To evaluate the surrogate models, a source-study-grouped evaluation protocol consisting of ten repeated train–test splits was employed. The compressive strength model obtained only moderate performance (R^2 = 0.654 ± 0.062), whereas the RCPT model exhibited unstable performance (R^2 = -1.01 ± 3.07) and was therefore not included in the optimisation constraints. An uncertainty-aware lower confidence bound was used for strength feasibility, and the buildability constraints were incorporated into NSGA-II. For the 40 MPa case, 20 separate runs resulted in a robust 15-member Pareto front with an 86.7% recurrence rate. The mixture chosen had estimated reductions of 50.0% in embodied carbon and 22.7% in material cost as compared with a baseline that had the same strength. Nevertheless, the benefits decreased as the strength floor was raised and became statistically no different from zero at 70 MPa. Experimental verification based on physical tests is necessary before the approach can be applied in practice. Repository Structure  * 1_data/: Processed concrete mix dataset (processed_dataset_1867_records.csv) and RCPT sub-dataset (rcpt_subset_203.csv).  * 2_code/: Python codebase including data_cleaner.py, train_catboost.py, nsga2_optimization.py, and run_full_pipeline.py.  * models/: Serialized .joblib CatBoost surrogate model binaries and uncertainty parameters.  * results/: Raw Pareto front outputs across 20 independent seed runs (pareto_front_seed_42.csv through seed_61.csv) and consolidated multi-run front metrics.  * Root: reproducibility_manifest.yaml, data_dictionary.csv, exclusion_log.csv, and main entrypoint run_all.py. Instructions for Reproducibility  * Extract concrete_mix_zenoda.zip.  * Install requirements: pip install -r 2_code/requirements.txt.  * Execute python run_all.py to re-run data cleaning, surrogate training, and multi-objective optimization.

items.summary: Traditional large language models (LLMs) are scoped to individual user sessions, limiting their knowledge to a single conversation and preventing them from learning user preferences that evolve over time. Existing agentic memory systems address this limitation but generally operate at the individual-user level, restricting the public knowledge that could be shared across users to improve downstream responses. We introduce AIM (Agentic Interoperable Memory), a unified, privacy-aware memory framework that enables multi-agent, multi-user LLM systems to persistently manage private and shared memory. AIM dynamically classifies information as private, scoped to one user and inaccessible to others, or public, accessible to all users. It enforces index-level access controls so that private memories are retrievable only by their owner, protecting sensitive data while allowing beneficial shared knowledge to improve coordination and consistency. We also introduce MUMBench (Multi-User Memory Benchmark), a dataset of multi-user interactions containing private and shareable information across four domains. To our knowledge, MUMBench is the first public dataset designed to evaluate multiple memory operations, including retrieval, creation, update, and deletion, in a multi-user environment. Across three independent runs on MUMBench, AIM achieves 96.0% visibility classification accuracy, 58.8% strict operation accuracy, and 70.5% state-aware operation accuracy.
items.title: AIM: A Privacy-Aware Interoperable Memory Framework for Multi-Agent Multi-User LLM Systems

items.summary: Research artifacts supporting the paper “Cybersecurity Investment Optimization Under Budget Constraints: From QUBO Formulation to Quantum Hardware”. This repository contains the source code, derived experimental instances, raw quantum measurement counts, QUBO/Ising models, QAOA execution outputs, transpiled-circuit metadata, backend information, job identifiers, and processed JSON/CSV results used to reproduce the experiments reported in the paper. The experiments implement an end-to-end cybersecurity investment optimization workflow based on a 0/1 Knapsack formulation transformed into QUBO and Ising representations and solved using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). The experimental design includes ideal simulation with Qiskit AerSimulator, architecture-aware noisy emulation using FakeKingston, and execution on the real IBM Quantum ibm_kingston Heron r2 processor. The artifact set covers the 12-qubit reference benchmark, the 20-qubit Safeguard-level stress experiment, and the real-hardware scaling series at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, and 156 logical qubits. For the scaling experiments, the decision variables beyond the original benchmark are explicitly constructed computational replicas used exclusively to evaluate circuit scaling, transpilation overhead, feasibility degradation, and real-QPU behavior; they must not be interpreted as distinct empirical cybersecurity controls. The repository preserves the information necessary to inspect and reproduce the experimental workflow, including optimized and transferred QAOA parameters, shot counts, sampled bitstrings, decoded cybersecurity portfolios, feasibility indicators, QUBO energies, circuit depths, gate counts, two-qubit gate counts, and real-hardware execution metadata. The public-evidence input dataset, CIS_MITRE_QAOA_Public_Evidence, is maintained separately on Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/andersonfpdossantos/cis-mitre-qaoa-public-evidence The dataset and these computational artifacts together provide the reproducibility package for the study. No claim of quantum advantage is made; the artifacts are intended to support independent verification, methodological replication, and further investigation of QAOA-based cybersecurity investment optimization.

items.summary: Lux AI Season 3 requires agents to act under partial observability, randomized episode level dynamics, and a best of five match structure that rewards both tactical execution and fast adaptation. We present HORIZON, a hierarchical agent that combines symmetry aware spatial perception, dual memory belief tracking, relic centric graph attention, information gain driven exploration, and an opponent conditioned policy mixture. HORIZON separates short horizon control from cross match meta reasoning, while auxiliary belief and world model objectives stabilize learning. Trained with PPO in a large scale JAX simulator, the resulting agent explicitly infers hidden game parameters and opponent style. Experiments show consistent gains in match win rate, episode win rate, adaptation gain, and league rating over strong recurrent and feed forward baselines.
items.title: Hierarchical Belief Modeling for Zero-Shot Opponent Adaptation in Partially Observable Multi-Agent Navigation

items.summary: AI coding assistants are becoming co-authors of production software, yet their evaluation centers on functional correctness, leaving open whether their code differs from human code in the quality dimensions dominating lifecycle cost. We compare human-written and AI-generated code at scale: 787,562 function pairs across Python, Java, and C, each human function mined from open-source repositories paired with implementations generated from its docstring by three AI assistants (OpenAI GPT models, DeepSeek-Coder, Qwen2.5-Coder). We characterize structural complexity and statistical naturalness, and map static-analysis findings onto Orthogonal Defect Classification for defects and the Common Weakness Enumeration for vulnerabilities, making authors and languages directly comparable. AI-generated code is structurally compressed and stylistically templated: roughly half the size and branching of human code, clustering apart at the style level. Defect profiles differ in kind: human code concentrates issues of mature codebases, AI code repetitive boilerplate; security is language-dependent, with LLMs producing more, and more severe, findings in Python and Java but fewer high-severity memory-safety findings than humans in C. Once size is controlled for, complexity metrics carry little signal, while naturalness separates authors. Finally, we release CQBench, a benchmark of 27,346 issue-prone tasks with baselines and an evaluation pipeline for quality assurance and security testing.
items.title: What is the Difference Between Me and You? Benchmarking the Quality Gap Between Human-Written and AI-Generated Code
